inventory_status_reason: The 12 entries below are verified bytes for the paths that are KNOWN to be deployed; each digest was captured by download and is trustworthy for those paths. They are still not an enumeration of the deployed asset set. Authenticated Cloudflare access is available (see deployment_target_observed), but neither Wrangler 4.134.0 nor an accessible API route exposes a listing of a static-assets Worker's deployed files, so the set cannot be enumerated from the platform side. The live version was uploaded from the Cloudflare Dashboard (source: "dash"), which means the authoritative asset set is the owner's uploaded website archive. Until that archive is supplied and reconciled, inventory_complete stays false and --require-complete-bundle refuses to certify a production bundle.
completion_requires: The owner's current website upload archive (the ZIP most recently uploaded to the carbonwebsite Dashboard), which is the authoritative asset set for the live version.
Reconciliation of that archive against the 12 verified digests below, so the archive is confirmed to be the deployed revision and not an older or newer one.
Addition of every archive path not already listed here, with its digest and byte size.
Then set inventory_status to "verified-complete" and inventory_complete to true, recording the archive's own digest as the provenance.

homepage_source_authority.note: Homepage source authority is the owner-supplied upload reconciled by --reconcile-owner-upload. It is deliberately kept separate from these read-only production observations. The index.html entry below records the CURRENT LIVE bytes so that an --existing-site copy can be verified; the production bundle intentionally REPLACES index.html with the integrated homepage.

release_authorization.note: Asset completeness is NOT release authorization. This manifest says only which bytes must survive a deployment. Publication and public activation remain governed by the release decision packet and the owner's named-operator authority.

assets.transport: GET https://carbonphysics.ai/ (the asset stored as index.html; /index.html 307-redirects to /)
GET https://carbonphysics.ai/workbench/ (the asset stored as workbench/index.html)

deployment_target_observed.rollback_target_note: 5a44ab03-ce7c-4100-ae42-71843b07246a is the version currently serving 100% of traffic and is therefore the rollback target for any deployment made now. The runbook previously named b99c37f0-c2d2-432b-842a-00b9fb518d96 (2026-09-09), which is two deployments older and is NOT the current predecessor. Re-capture the live version immediately before deploying; do not reuse either ID from a document.

routing_configuration.source: authenticated `wrangler versions view --json` on carbonwebsite version 5a44ab03-ce7c-4100-ae42-71843b07246a (2026-09-20)
routing_configuration.implication: auto-trailing-slash is why /index.html 307-redirects to / and /workbench/index.html 307-redirects to /workbench/. Any preservation recipe that downloads the literal path "index.html" captures an empty redirect body. not_found_handling "none" is why favicon.ico, robots.txt, _headers, _redirects and _routes.json all return 404: they are absent assets, not routing rules.

routing_observed_note: Superseded by routing_configuration above, which was read from the deployed version rather than inferred from responses.

blocked_on.what: Enumeration of the complete deployed asset set.
blocked_on.why_not_resolved_by_login: Cloudflare authentication is present and sufficient for deployment (workers / workers_scripts / workers_routes write). The gap is capability, not credentials: there is no Wrangler command that lists a static-assets Worker's deployed files.
blocked_on.owner_action: Supply the website archive most recently uploaded to the carbonwebsite Cloudflare Dashboard.
